mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain positive despite multiple FEDFUNDS > 5.25% events; or IC > 0.05 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls surprise exceeding 50,000 jobs (PAYEMS) coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong labor demand supports corporate optimism and equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: In regimes with high inflation, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero after PAYEMS > 50,000 events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% in two consecutive months predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as weak manufacturing demand reduces corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2% in two consecutive months
regime_hint: Early-cycle soft landing turning into recession risk
failure_condition: Over 12 months, 60-day forward returns remain positive despite INDPRO double-dip below trend; or IC < 0.01 in out-of-sample.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 0.2% for three months indicates a disinflationary environment that lowers growth expectations and produces a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: During periods of strong economic growth, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after three consecutive CPIAUCSL < 0.2% months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains below 1%, it signals a dual accommodative signal that is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes, 60-day forward returns do not outperform a risk-free rate proxy by at least 1% after the trigger (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in retail sales employment (HOUST) by more than 5,000 units coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as rising labor demand in retail supports optimism about consumer spending.
failure_condition: Over 30 days, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive after HOUST > 5,000 events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by at least 3% generate a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals accelerating supply-side momentum that feeds demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA by ≥3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In deflationary regimes, 20-day forward returns do not beat the risk-free rate after INDPRO acceleration (IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in monthly retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual: if HOUST falls by ≥10% month-over-month for two months) predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects deteriorating consumer demand and compression in profit margins.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by ≥10% from previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of low inflation, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative after the double decline in HOUST (p > 0.10).
